seo_description: Three Wwise middleware projects: voice management, spatial audio, and cross-platform memory optimization.

hero.title: Three Wwise Projects
hero.lead: Three school projects where I learned Wwise by hitting real problems. Voice limits in a zombie shooter. Zone-based audio transitions. Fitting everything into 15 MB on Android.
hero.context: Solo projects from DAE (2021-2024). Not shipped games—school assignments. But I treated them seriously: tracked memory, hit platform limits, wrote integration code.

section.title: The Projects
section.subtitle: Three different problems that forced me to learn how Wwise actually works.

boney.title: Boney Boogaloo
boney.p1: Zombie wave shooter. Max 5 enemies at once. First time I used Wwise.
boney.p2: Kept hitting the 256 voice limit. Player shoots non-stop, zombies keep spawning. I made random containers—6 gunshot variations, 6 spawn sounds. Stops it from feeling repetitive.
boney.p3: Balanced volumes in Wwise. Gunshots at -2dB, player hurt sounds at +4dB, zombies at -5dB. Trimmed silence from files, used ADPCM compression.
boney.p4: 44 sounds in 9 random containers. All 2D. No effects. Straight to Master Bus.
boney.video_caption: Every gunshot sounds different. Max 5 zombies on screen.

ellen.title: Ellen
ellen.p1: Platformer with magic combat. First time I tried spatial audio.
ellen.p2: I wrote 10 attenuation curves. Enemies heard from 25m, footsteps from 75m, explosions from 100m. Footsteps switch based on surface—raycasts detect the floor type.
ellen.p3: Ambient changes per zone using State groups. Layers crossfade over 6.5 seconds when you move. I set up 4 reverb buses for different room sizes.
ellen.p4: Compression: Music at Q8 OGG, ambience Q7, SFX Q5, voice ADPCM.
ellen.video_caption: Spatial audio with dynamic reverb and surface switching.

stomach.title: Stomach Aches
stomach.p1: FPS platformer inside a human body. Three zones—Brain, Mouth, Stomach. Had to run on cheap Android phones with 2GB RAM.
stomach.p2: Android audio budget: 15MB total. I set up zone-based loading. Only current zone's sounds stay in memory. Brain 670KB, Mouth 384KB, Stomach 2.8MB.
stomach.p3: I used Wwise's Silence plugin instead of real silent files. Saved 80% memory. Waterfall has 3 layers that blend by distance using RTPC: Close 130KB, Mid 6.3MB, Far 3.6MB.
stomach.p4: Footsteps switch per material. Music streams from disk to save RAM. Had to fix loops so sounds don't get stuck playing.
stomach.video_caption: Waterfall layers blend as you get closer. Zone loading keeps memory under 15MB.

learned.title: What I Learned
learned.subtitle: Skills from fixing things when they broke
learned.skill1_desc: Staying under the 256 voice limit. Tracking memory budgets. Picking compression that doesn't trash quality.
learned.skill2_desc: Writing distance curves for different sound types. Positioning audio in 3D. Making sounds fade at the right distance.
learned.skill3_desc: Hooking game events to Wwise. Making audio respond to player position and game state without hardcoding everything.
learned.skill4_desc: What loads now, what streams from disk, what unloads when you change zones. Staying under 15MB on Android.
learned.skill5_desc: Writing C# scripts that talk to the Wwise API. Handling zone triggers. Fixing sounds that don't stop playing.
learned.skill6_desc: Different compression for PC vs mobile. Testing on emulators. Profiling memory before it breaks in production.
